description: Game Design teaches how games are made: analyzing games and play value, design terms, intellectual property, experimenting with rules, designing and prototyping your own game, playtesting with real players, and meeting game development professionals.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Analyzing games
requirements.summary: Analyzing games from different media and the kinds of play value they offer.

requirements.title: Design terms
requirements.summary: Game design terms and how they apply to specific games.

requirements.title: Intellectual property
requirements.summary: What intellectual property is, how it is protected, and licensed properties in games.

requirements.title: Changing the rules
requirements.summary: Playing a game, then testing and comparing rule changes.

requirements.title: Designing a game
requirements.summary: A vision statement, preliminary rules and drawings in a design notebook.

requirements.title: Prototype and playtest
requirements.summary: Building a prototype, playtesting and revising the rules.

requirements.title: Instructions and feedback
requirements.summary: Writing instructions, watching new players use them, and reviewing their feedback.

requirements.title: Meeting a professional
requirements.summary: One option: visiting a game development professional or educator.
